newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua cenbank pleads workers not to strike.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua cenbank pleads workers not to strike.

text.p: Nicaraguan Central Bank President Noel Ramirez on Friday called on Nicaraguans to ignore a national strike call by the left-wing Sandinista Front and let the government's economic program work.

Ramirez told a news conference that the strike, called for Monday, would threaten the economic growth and stability produced by free-market policies of President Arnoldo Aleman's government, which took power on January 10.
Since Aleman's inauguration, Central Bank reserves in Nicaragua have grown by $60 million, reflecting growing foreign investor confidence in Nicaragua, he said.
"We cannot risk this confidence with behaviors that alter the public order and it is therefore important that the Nicaraguan people firmly demand that this confidence not be put in danger," he said.
Sandinista leaders said the protest would include transportation and public workers strikes, protest marches and and roadblocks to paralyze traffic across the country.

Former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega has said the strike was to protest the government's "dictatorial attitudes," and demand changes in its economic policy and a just solution to Nicaragua's bitter property dispute.
It will be the first major challenge to the right-wing government by the Sandinistas, whose activists are know for their boisterous social protest.
Ramirez, along with Nicaragua's largest business groups, have issued public statements calling on Nicaraguans to ignore the strike call for fear of undermining budding investor confidence.
